text: None — every rule is carried by the bean table: name is required, age is a whole number between 0 and 150. The platform enforces and tests these.

comments.text: The Requirements section asserts age is a "whole number", but the bean table's declared rules (per the derived artifacts) are only min(0) and max(150) — nothing enforces integrality. If the age field's kind is a general number, a value like 32.5 would pass validation. Either declare an integrality/format rule in the bean table's notes so the platform enforces and tests it, or drop "whole number" from the requirement so the stated rule matches what is actually carried.

Resolved by the entity descriptor: Person.age is stored as fieldType INTEGER, so integrality IS carried by the bean table — the number kind maps to a whole-number field and a value like 32.5 cannot be persisted, independent of the min/max rules. The Requirements line therefore states exactly what the table carries; no extra rule is needed.

Clarification for review: there are intentionally no numbered requirements — no cross-record rule, process rule or external check exists for this register, and restating the table rules (name required; age 0–150, whole number) as R1..Rn would duplicate what the platform already enforces and tests.

text: Out: age auto-derivation from a date of birth — only an explicit age is held.

comments.text: Clarification for review: age is stored exactly as entered — there is no date-of-birth field, so a stored age does not change as the person ages and must be updated by hand. This is a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight; if a reviewer sees drift risk here, that is the trade-off the author accepted.

Clarification for review: min(0)/max(150) are sanity bounds, not a business rule from the request. Integrality is carried by the storage type — the entity descriptor declares age as INTEGER, so fractional values cannot be persisted (see the resolved reviewer thread on this).

text: A register of natural persons, each recorded with a name and an age. It serves any signed-in user of the deployment who needs to create, browse and edit person records.
